pages.quiz:
AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Ice melting to water

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Aquaculture? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Aquaculture.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Aquaculture.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Aquaculture.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Aquaculture.

4. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

5. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Overgrazing continuously

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Rearing Selected Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Rearing Selected Animals.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Rearing Selected Animals.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Rearing Selected Animals.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Rearing Selected Animals.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Inorganic fertilisers? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Inorganic fertilisers.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Inorganic fertilisers.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Inorganic fertilisers.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Inorganic fertilisers.

8. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

9. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Protection: Pest control? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Protection: Pest control.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Protection: Pest control.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Protection: Pest control.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Pest control.

11. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

12. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Digestive systems of animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Health: Parasite control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Structures in Animal production and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Aquaculture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Ice melting to water

2. A — Glucose and oxygen

3. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Aquaculture.

4. A — 100 °C

5. B — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

6. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Rearing Selected Animals.

7. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Inorganic fertilisers.

8. B — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

9. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

10. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Pest control.

11. A — newton (N)

12. B — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Digestive systems of animals; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Animal Health: Parasite control; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Structures in Animal production; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Aquaculture; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
